text:
maria (AE): Heads up — Colossus Health asked for an acceptance matrix for throughput/latency. They want sustained 120 qps with p99 < 350ms, ability to burst to 800 qps for ~2m windows, and KMS in the request path. Can SEs run a test this week?

sam (SE): I can run it Thurs. Proposed plan: 30m soak at 120 qps, plus 3x 2-min microbursts to 800 qps spaced 5m apart. Compare two variants: baseline f32 model and 4-bit quantized + KV cache. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, GPU util, queue depth, and per-token cost delta.

raj (SRE): Note: our prior KMS tests added ~6-12ms per request on p50 and larger on tail when concurrent decrypts pile up. Need to confirm TLS termination (ALB) vs passthrough from their side — that changes measurements.

maria (AE): They require KMS + VPC peering. Also sales needs a clear cost delta for burst: what to reserve vs run on-demand. Can you include both Dedicated reserved estimate and Hosted burst pricing?

zoe (ops): Ops can spin up a temporary dedicated pool for the window: 4xA100 + 1 standby, configured with batching target=16 and max concurrency per GPU. That should handle sustained 120 qps and 800 qps microbursts. I'll schedule infra and open the ports for the load generator.

sam (SE): Load generator commands I'll use (for reproducibility):
```bash
# soak 30m at 120 qps
hey -z 30m -c 250 -q 120 -m POST -d '{"prompt":"<redacted>"}' https://staging-api.redwood/v1/generate
# microburst (2m) to 800 qps, run 3 times
for i in 1 2 3; do hey -z 2m -c 1000 -q 800 -m POST -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://staging-api.redwood/v1/generate; sleep 300; done
```
Will also collect GPU metrics (nvidia-smi sample), kernel fallback logs, and proxy request traces.

ops-bot: deploy: dedicated-pool-colossus-1912 started (provisioning), ETA 14m.

sam (SE): Quick notes after today's run: baseline f32 p99 (no KMS) ~280ms; enabling KMS bumped p99 to ~330-420ms with occasional spikes. Quantized variant: p99 steady-state ~470ms, but during bursts we saw p99 push to ~620ms due to kernel fallback and increased queueing. GPU util: baseline ~72% during soak, peaked ~95% during bursts. CPU/network queueing observed on the host at burst peaks (~40% sustained).

raj (SRE): Correlated spikes with concurrent KMS decrypt calls visible in traces. Suggestions: pre-warm KMS tokens, enable async decrypt at the edge proxy so token ops don't block the critical path, and increase proxy worker threads during bursts. That trimmed ~8-12ms off p99 in a quick rerun.

maria (AE): Sales wants numbers for pricing. Draft estimate: Dedicated reserved (monthly) for that pool ~"$9,500/month" (4xA100 + ops overhead) — temporary test window prorate ~"$1,200" for multi-hour run. Hosted burst pricing alternative: additional peak capacity charge estimated at "$0.10/peak-qps-minute" (works out to ~$80 for a single 2m 800-qps burst). Also include token-cost delta: quantized model saved ~18% token cost but added ~6% infra overhead; net token+infra savings ~12% on expected volume. Please treat these as draft numbers for negotiation.

zoe (ops): Blockers for go-live flagged in their security questionnaire: key custody details, HSM requirement, and audit log retention windows. They also want canary rollout with automatic fallback to a smaller model variant on SLA breach.

raj (SRE): I'll take the security Q items. Plan: propose HSM-backed KMS (Private deployment option) and provide log-retention options (30/90/365 days). Also include a canary rollout recipe (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with health checks) and automatic fallback on sustained p99 > 500ms.

maria (AE): Great — next steps: sam to write a short runbook + attach results snapshot, zoe to share infra cost/prorate numbers, raj to draft security answers and canary recipe. I'll schedule follow-up with the customer on Friday 10am PT.

sam (SE): I'll post the runbook and a 1-page results summary in this thread (charts + CSV). TL;DR numbers: baseline f32 p99 = 280ms, quant p99 steady = 470ms, quant p99 peak = 620ms. Token cost: baseline $0.018/token-equivalent, quant saved ~18% -> effective $0.0147, but infra overhead raises net effective cost reduction to ~12%.

maria (AE): Perfect — I'll loop in the customer and send the acceptance matrix + price note. :thumbsup:

zoe (ops): Infra postmortem & cost breakdown will be attached in the follow-up.

raj (SRE): I'll attach the security Q draft by EOD tomorrow.

maria (AE): Thanks all — really helpful.
